lens: F — the vault and the containment claim (`contracts/src/**`, proposal §7.1, `docs/gate-s2-evidence.md`)

findings.title: The corrected §7.1 containment claim is still false in the dimension it says it bounds: the wei ceiling is per-ACTION, and a compromised signer drains the vault's whole native balance
findings.surface: Sentinel_Protocol_Lab_Proposal_v0_2.md:661 (§7.1 bullet, D-042 correction) and :238 (§4); carried by contracts/src/SentinelVault.sol:303 and by docs/gate-s2-evidence.md §11 / scripts/test.sh:577-585
findings.claim: The D-042 correction says: "the hard caps bound the NATIVE-VALUE dimension only. Pause, nonce, deadline and the vault's own wei ceiling are enforced onchain... Token authority is not capped by the vault at all." The repair generalised the DEMONSTRATION (ERC20 approve) and not the ARGUMENT. `maxNativeValueWei` is compared once per action (`SentinelVault.sol:303`) and nothing anywhere — vault, PolicyPayload, or MandatePayload — carries a cumulative, rate-limited or velocity bound. Under the exact threat model the bullet names ("Evaluator or signer compromise scenario"), the native dimension is therefore NOT bounded: the compromised signer mints one receipt per nonce at exactly the ceiling and the vault's entire native balance leaves. The other three items in the same list are no better against that threat: `actionNonce` prevents replay but not a fresh receipt for N+1, and `deadline` and `receipt.expiresAt` are fields the compromised signer chooses (`type(uint64).max` is accepted). Of the four items listed as the residual onchain containment, only PAUSE (an owner reaction) bounds a compromised signer — and the two checks that genuinely do bound one, the target and selector allowlists, are omitted from the list. §4:238 carries the same claim uncorrected: "the lab limits worst-case blast radius to testnet funds and the vault's hard constraints". This also makes A-040's recorded harm bound for the codeless-target defect — "stranding up to the per-action ceiling" — false as a bound: the strandable amount is the vault's whole native balance, one ceiling at a time, unbounded in count.
findings.why_it_matters: §7.1's bullet exists to state what containment survives evaluator/signer compromise; it is the sentence a hostile reader goes to first, and it was already corrected once for overstating exactly this. A reader takes "the hard caps bound the NATIVE-VALUE dimension" to mean native loss is bounded below the vault's balance. It is not. The v1.1 register (line 152) records only a per-action ALLOWANCE ceiling as the owed fix, so the native half of the same hole is not on any list.
findings.reproduction:
cp <scratchpad>/DrainProbe.t.sol <worktree>/contracts/test/DrainProbe.t.sol ; export PATH="$HOME/.foundry/bin:$PATH"; cd <worktree>/contracts && forge test --match-contract DrainProbe -vv

Observed:
  [PASS] test_PROBE_CONTROL_singleActionOverCapIsRefused() (gas: 54136)
  [PASS] test_PROBE_capIsPerActionNotPerVault() (gas: 6726280)
  Suite result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped

The probe builds a vault with maxNativeValueWei = 0.01 ether and a balance of 1 ether, allowlists DemoPay + purchase only, then executes 100 sequential ALLOW receipts each with valueWei == 0.01 ether (exactly the cap, never rejected), deadline = type(uint64).max, expiresAt = type(uint64).max, relayed by address(0xDEAD) (no key), warping 365 days between every action. Final asserts that hold: vault.actionNonce() == 100, address(vault).balance == 0, address(demoPay).balance == 1 ether. The CONTROL in the same file confirms one action at cap+1 still reverts with ValueOverCap and moves nothing — so the drain is measured against a vault whose cap is live, not against a vault with no cap.

Honest qualification I verified rather than assumed: with the lab's own allowlist the drained ETH lands in DemoPay, which has no withdrawal — so this is total, irrecoverable LOSS of the vault's native balance rather than attacker gain. It becomes theft the moment any allowlisted target forwards value.
findings.probe_moved_something: vault.actionNonce() 0 -> 100 and address(vault).balance 1 ether -> 0, with address(demoPay).balance 0 -> 1 ether. The CONTROL in the same file moves nothing and reverts with ValueOverCap, which separates "the cap does not bound aggregate loss" from "the cap is not enforced at all".

findings.title: The D-042 invariant repair is silently reversible and its verifying mutation ships nowhere: deleting one line leaves 73/73 green and restores the exact pre-repair blind spot
findings.claim: `invariant_futureNonceNeverExecutes` was added by D-042 because the `actionNonce != actionNonce` -> `<` weakening survived all ten prior invariants. A-040 records that the first attempt at this repair FAILED silently because the selector was not registered, and calls that "the project's most-repeated defect appearing inside the fix for a finding about the same defect". That failure mode is still completely undefended: (a) deleting or re-pointing line 703 leaves the whole Foundry suite at 73/73 green, because the only test that exercises `executeFutureNonce` calls it directly (`test_nonVacuity_futureNonceAndFailingCallArmsAreReachable`) rather than asserting it is registered; and (b) the future-nonce mutation itself exists NOWHERE in the repository — `scripts/mutate.sh` S1–S25 contains no mutation of `if (action.actionNonce != actionNonce) revert BadNonce();`, and neither does the reviewer artifact `sol_mutants.json` it was promoted from — so `scripts/mutate.sh` cannot re-run it either. `scripts/test.sh:586-589`, `docs/decisions.md` A-040, and `docs/gate-s2-evidence.md` §11 all state "both of those mutations are now killed, verified by re-running them". Only one of the two (the failed-external-call mutation, S23) actually ships. `scripts/mutate.sh`'s own header states the standard this violates: "a claim resting on a script nobody else has cannot be independently reproduced."
findings.why_it_matters: Gate 6's marginal evidence — the one thing D-042 added to a campaign measured at zero marginal killing power — rests on a single unguarded line of test-harness wiring plus a mutation that no shipped instrument contains. The one previously-observed regression of exactly this shape is undetectable today, and the published verification of the repair is not reproducible from the repository.

  (S1–S25 enumerated at scripts/mutate.sh:825-1010; sol_mutants.json holds 20 entries, S1–S20, none about the nonce comparison.)

(2) The repair is silently reversible:

  cd contracts && forge test
  -> "Ran 5 test suites in 36.96s: 73 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (73 total tests)"

(3) With the arm de-registered, apply the vault mutation `if (action.actionNonce != actionNonce)` -> `if (action.actionNonce < actionNonce)` and run the campaign alone:

  -> "Suite result: ok. 11 passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped"   (pre-D-042 state exactly: the invariant is green and pointing at nothing)

(4) Control proving the mutation and the invariant are both live, with sel[12] restored:
  -> "[FAIL: a receipt pinned to an unreached nonce executed - future-nonce authorization] invariant_futureNonceNeverExecutes()" and "Suite result: FAILED. 9 passed; 2 failed"

Both files were restored afterwards; `git diff --stat -- contracts/src contracts/test` is empty and `forge test` is 73/73.
findings.probe_moved_something: Step (3) moved the campaign from FAILED (2 failed) to ok (11 passed) on the same mutated vault, purely from the one-line de-registration — so the probe demonstrably toggled the campaign's killing power rather than reading a constant. Step (4) is the paired control that shows the mutation is not inert.

findings.title: Measured: the repaired campaign still cannot construct a violation of ANY of the vault's twelve action- and receipt-validation checks — 12/12 mutations survive all eleven invariants
findings.surface: contracts/test/SentinelVault.invariants.t.sol:355-380 (`VaultHandler._bundle`), :340-352 (`_data`), :686-705 (selector registration); claim surface docs/gate-s2-evidence.md §7 "Boundary, and it moved this session... It now covers both."
findings.claim: The lens asks what the handler still cannot build. Answer, measured: `_bundle` hardcodes six of the eleven ActionPayload fields to always-valid values (chainId = block.chainid, vault = address(vault), target = address(demoPay), operation = CALL, mandateHash/policyHash = the active ones, deadline = now + 1h) and bounds valueWei to [1, 0.01 ether] against a cap of exactly 0.01 ether; `_data` always emits a well-formed `DemoPay.purchase` selector; the receipt always names `vault.signer()` with expiresAt = now + 30m; and no handler action ever revokes the mandate or policy. Consequently twelve distinct vault checks are unreachable by the campaign at any call count. Each of the twelve, disabled one at a time, survives all 11 invariants (16,384 calls each) and is caught by the deterministic tests: value cap, target allowlist, selector allowlist, operation, chainId, vault, action deadline, receipt expiry, activeMandateHash zero-guard, activePolicyHash zero-guard, calldata-length, named-signer. This corroborates rather than contradicts `scripts/test.sh`'s recorded boundary ("the deterministic tests carry it and the campaign corroborates"), which is why I score it MEDIUM — but `docs/gate-s2-evidence.md` §7 states the boundary only in terms of the two EXECUTION PATHS and closes with "It now covers both", which reads as a closed gap. The gap is a check-coverage gap, and it is total on the hard backstops the same document elsewhere calls the containment story.
findings.why_it_matters: Gate 6 is "fuzz and invariant tests cannot bypass SentinelVault". The measured marginal contribution of the stateful campaign to the vault's twelve validation checks is zero, and the cause is structural (unconstructible inputs), not statistical — so no profile depth changes it. §7 of the evidence pack should carry the number, not a path-shaped boundary.
findings.reproduction:
export PATH="$HOME/.foundry/bin:$PATH"
Baseline first, on the untouched tree:
  cd contracts && forge test  -> 73 passed, 0 failed
  forge test --match-contract SentinelVaultInvariantTest --match-test "invariant_"  -> 11 passed, 0 failed (48.20s)

Then the sweep (driver and results retained at <scratchpad>/{mutate_vault.py,sweep.sh,sweep-results.txt}). Each mutation appends `&& false` to one condition (or drops the zero-guard disjunct), asserted to apply by an exact-count anchor check printed as "APPLIED <name>: <old> -> <new>", then runs:
  forge test --no-match-contract SentinelVaultInvariantTest
  forge test --match-contract SentinelVaultInvariantTest --match-test "invariant_"

Result, all twelve identical:
  DETERMINISTIC: "Encountered a total of 1 failing tests, 56 tests succeeded"
  CAMPAIGN:      "Suite result: ok. 11 passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped"
  grep -c 'CAMPAIGN: Suite result: ok. 11 passed' sweep-results.txt -> 12
  grep -c 'DETERMINISTIC: Encountered a total of 1 failing' sweep-results.txt -> 12

Mutations: M1 valueWei>cap, M2 allowedTarget, M3 allowedSelector, M4 operation!=CALL, M5 chainId, M6 vault, M7 action.deadline, M8 receipt.expiresAt, M9 activeMandateHash zero-guard, M10 callData.length<4, M11 receipt.signer!=signer, M12 activePolicyHash zero-guard. Tree restored (md5 of SentinelVault.sol back to b3ab093103276f36ddb327b6ffcedebc; forge test 73/73).

Profile caveat, stated because it bounds the claim: I ran the DEFAULT profile (256 runs x 64 depth = 16,384 calls/invariant), not `--gate` (262,144). Depth cannot change these twelve — the fields are hardcoded in `_bundle`, so the violating input is not merely rare, it is unconstructible.
findings.probe_moved_something: Each mutation moved the deterministic suite from 73/73 green to exactly one failure, in twelve different tests, while the campaign's 11/11 stayed constant — so the probes were live and the constant is the campaign's, not the harness's. The paired future-nonce run (F-VAULT-2 step 4) proves this campaign CAN be made to fail, so "11 passed" is not a dead reading.

findings.title: `invariant_ownerAndCapsAreImmutableFromExecution` cannot fail for any behaviour: both fields it checks are write-once, and it is evaluated at environment setup
findings.surface: contracts/test/SentinelVault.invariants.t.sol:900; contracts/src/SentinelVault.sol:118 (`uint256 public immutable maxNativeValueWei`), :149 (the only assignment to `owner`)
findings.claim: The invariant asserts `vault.owner() == vm.addr(OWNER_PK)` and `vault.maxNativeValueWei() == 0.01 ether`. `maxNativeValueWei` is `immutable`, so no bytecode can write it; `owner` has exactly one assignment in the whole contract (constructor, line 149) and there is no `transferOwnership` or any other setter. No handler action, no call sequence, and no execution path can falsify either conjunct — the assertion is guaranteed by the language and by the absence of a write path, not by the property its name claims ("immutable FROM EXECUTION"). The liveness probe also shows Foundry evaluates it in the setup phase (`runs: 0, calls: 0`), i.e. before any sequence is explored. Meanwhile the four pieces of owner-controlled state that CAN move — `signer`, `activeMandateHash`, `activePolicyHash`, `paused` — are not covered by it.
findings.why_it_matters: One of eleven invariants is unfalsifiable, so the campaign's headline count of ten/eleven invariants overstates by one what is actually being tested. This is the project's own recorded pattern (an instrument that exists and points at something other than what it names), inside the instrument that carries Gate 6.
findings.reproduction:
Structural, on the unmutated tree:
  grep -n 'owner *=' contracts/src/SentinelVault.sol  -> only line 149 (constructor)
  grep -n 'immutable' contracts/src/SentinelVault.sol -> line 118, maxNativeValueWei
  (no `transferOwnership` / owner setter exists anywhere in the file)

Empirical corroboration: across all twelve mutations of F-VAULT-3, each disabling a different vault check, this invariant passed every time.

Liveness probe (proving it does run, so the pass is not a skip):
  change line 900's `assertEq(vault.maxNativeValueWei(), 0.01 ether);` to `0.02 ether`
  forge test --match-contract SentinelVaultInvariantTest --match-test "invariant_ownerAndCaps"
  -> "[FAIL: failed to set up invariant testing environment: assertion failed: 10000000000000000 != 20000000000000000] invariant_ownerAndCapsAreImmutableFromExecution() (runs: 0, calls: 0, reverts: 0)"
  The "runs: 0, calls: 0" and "failed to set up invariant testing environment" wording is itself the evidence that this assertion is decided before the campaign explores anything. File restored (md5 39da1edd54d5919c371547b01214cec6).
findings.probe_moved_something: The liveness probe moved the invariant from PASS to FAIL, proving it is registered and executed; the failure text moved the reported phase to "failed to set up invariant testing environment ... runs: 0, calls: 0", which is the fact the finding rests on.

findings.title: The docstring justifying permissionless `execute` rests on owner authority the automatic path never checks
findings.claim: Line 21 states: "a relayer can only cause what the owner already authorized, exactly once." On the automatic path the vault verifies no owner signature at all — `owner` is used only by `onlyOwner` and by the override path's `digest.recover(ownerSig) != owner`. `activateMandate` takes a bare `bytes32` with no signature check, and `MandatePayload.principal` (which `SentinelTypes.sol` says "must equal the vault owner at activation time") is never seen onchain. What `executeWithReceipt` actually checks is the SIGNER's authorization. Under the compromise model §7.1 names — the model this whole contract exists to bound — a relayer causes what the compromised signer authorized, and the sentence is the security argument for having no caller check at all. "exactly once" is true; "what the owner already authorized" has no onchain referent.
findings.why_it_matters: This is a comment stating a property the code does not have, placed where it justifies removing a control. The project has recorded six of these in one session (A-044) and one of them was reused as evidence in a later entry. The design decision is defensible; the stated reason is not the one the code implements.
findings.reproduction:
Read on the unmutated tree:
  sed -n '16,23p' contracts/src/SentinelVault.sol      -> the claim
  grep -n 'owner' contracts/src/SentinelVault.sol      -> every use of `owner` is `onlyOwner`, the constructor, `SignerRotated`/events, or `digest.recover(ownerSig) != owner` inside executeWithOverride; nothing in executeWithReceipt or _checkAction/_checkReceipt
  grep -n 'principal' contracts/src/SentinelVault.sol   -> no output (the field exists only in SentinelTypes.sol:MandatePayload)
Also demonstrated by F-VAULT-1's probe, in which address(0xDEAD) relays 100 executions the owner never signed anything for.
findings.probe_moved_something: No mutation needed — this is a read of shipped source against shipped prose. The corroborating execution is F-VAULT-1's probe, which moved actionNonce 0 -> 100 under a relayer with no key and no owner signature anywhere in the transaction.

brief_critique:
Two problems, one of which cost me nothing and one of which would have cost a literal-minded reviewer the round's best finding.

1. THE DOCUMENT SCOPE IS TOO NARROW AND REPEATS THE FAILURE MODE IT WARNS ABOUT. The brief scopes the containment claims to "`Sentinel_Protocol_Lab_Proposal_v0_2.md` §7.1 and `docs/gate-s2-evidence.md`". The same containment claim also lives at proposal §4 (line 238: "the lab limits worst-case blast radius to testnet funds and the vault's hard constraints"), in `scripts/test.sh`'s WHAT IS NOT COVERED block (lines 577-589), and in the vault's own contract-level docstring. D-042 corrected §7.1 and left §4 untouched. A reviewer who took the scope literally would find F-VAULT-1, correct §7.1 a second time, and leave §4 stating the identical thing — which is failure mode 3 from the standing brief (generalise the demonstration, not the argument) reproduced by the brief itself, on the exact finding class the brief was written to chase.

2. THE INVARIANT HALF POINTS AT THE CAMPAIGN AND NOT AT ITS EVIDENCE. The brief says "Two arms were added. Measure what this one can still not build." I did (F-VAULT-3), and the answer largely CORROBORATES what `scripts/test.sh` already records honestly — so that instruction, followed alone, yields a medium finding restating a known limit. My strongest instrument finding (F-VAULT-2) is in `scripts/mutate.sh` and in one line of selector registration, neither of which the brief names, and it is about whether the repair the brief cites can be re-verified at all. If the lens is "does the campaign carry Gate 6", the mutation harness that measures the campaign is inside the lens and should have been named.

3. Minor, and in the brief's favour: the warning that one answer (`approve` / token authority) is already recorded and must not be re-reported was load-bearing. Without it I would probably have spent the round rediscovering it, since it is the first thing the contract's shape suggests. Naming the recorded answer and demanding "the NEXT one" is the single most useful sentence in the lens brief.

coverage_statement:
SWEPT TO THE BOTTOM: `contracts/src/SentinelVault.sol` line by line — every check in `_checkAction`, `_checkReceipt`, `_consumeAndCall`, both entry points, the override binding, all six owner-only functions, the reentrancy modifier, and every state variable's write paths (I enumerated the assignments to `owner` and confirmed `maxNativeValueWei` is `immutable`). `contracts/src/types/SentinelTypes.sol` read fully for what each payload does and does not carry — I checked specifically that no payload at any layer (Mandate, Policy, Action) has a cumulative, velocity, or budget field, which is what F-VAULT-1 rests on. Both demo contracts read fully. `contracts/test/SentinelVault.invariants.t.sol` read fully, including the handler's every action and the selector registration; I derived the campaign's constructible-input set from `_bundle` and `_data` and then MEASURED it with twelve mutations rather than reasoning about it.

SWEPT AT THE SURFACE: `SentinelVault.t.sol` and `SentinelVault.backstops.t.sol` — I indexed every test function and read the tamper block and the three `test_LIMIT_*` tests closely, and confirmed by error-selector grep that all twelve checks I mutated have a named deterministic test. I did NOT read the other ~30 deterministic tests line by line, so I cannot say whether any of them is itself misaimed; my sweep shows only that each of the twelve mutations produced exactly one failure somewhere.

NOT TOUCHED AT ALL, and these are real holes in this lens: `SentinelTypes.t.sol` (386 lines pinning the typehashes) — the encoding was cleared by a 4-way differential in A-040 and I took that on the record rather than re-running it. The corpus vault configuration (A-040's ecrecover-precompile allowlist defect) — I quoted it as corroboration but did not re-verify the config or check whether it has been repaired; if it has not, F-VAULT-1's drain lands in a codeless precompile. The TypeScript evaluator's and the D-010 verifier's view of the vault's caps. `ts/test/cases.e2e.test.ts` and `propose.e2e.test.ts`, which are the only place the vault is exercised against a real deployment and the only place the live allowlist contents would be visible — I never established what targets and selectors the shipped e2e vault actually allowlists, which bounds how confidently anyone should read F-VAULT-1's stranded-vs-stolen qualification. The gate profile. `scripts/test.sh` and `scripts/mutate.sh` executed end to end (I read both and ran neither).

A NULL RESULT WORTH RECORDING RATHER THAN LEAVING IMPLICIT: I went looking for a second EXPLOITABLE gap of the `approve` class — something one valid ALLOW receipt buys beyond one capped call — and did not find one. The cross-product of the target and selector allowlists is the obvious candidate and is already recorded (A-040); with the lab's one-target/one-selector configuration it is inert, and I confirmed the vault admits no delegatecall, no self-call reaching an owner control, and no reentrant second consumption. The residual containment gap I could demonstrate is aggregate rather than per-receipt, and it needs signer compromise — which is why F-VAULT-1 is filed as a false claim about a bound and not as a bypass.
